summary: A Zee Business explainer on India's history in Cricket World Cup semi-finals ahead of the 2023 semi-final against New Zealand at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai on November 15. It notes this is India's seventh semi-final appearance and, after the Sri Lanka win, India had booked their place. It recaps each earlier semi-final from 1983 to 2019, covering venues, opponents, top performers and results.
one_line: Recap of India's six previous Cricket World Cup semi-finals (1983-2019) ahead of their seventh, against New Zealand at Wankhede in 2023.
key_facts: India booked a 2023 semi-final place by beating Sri Lanka by 302 runs at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai on November 2, 2023.
The 2023 semi-final against New Zealand is at Wankhede Stadium on Wednesday, November 15; it is India's seventh World Cup semi-final.
In their last six World Cups, India have reached the semi-finals five times.

1983: India beat England by six wickets in Manchester on June 22, with 5.2 overs to spare; Mohinder Amarnath was Man-of-the-Match and Sandeep Patil hit 51 not out in 32 balls. India went on to win the tournament.
1987: India lost to England by 35 runs at Wankhede on November 5; Graham Gooch scored 115 in 136 balls and England made 254 for 6.

1996: At Eden Gardens on March 13, India collapsed to 120 for 8 in 34.1 overs chasing 251 after Sachin Tendulkar fell for 65, and the match was called off after crowd trouble, giving Sri Lanka the win.
2003: India beat Kenya by 91 runs in Durban on March 20; Sourav Ganguly made an unbeaten 111 in 114 balls and Zaheer Khan took 3 for 14.
2011: India beat Pakistan in Mohali on March 30; Tendulkar scored 85, India made 260 for 9 and Pakistan were all out for 231. India then beat Sri Lanka to win their second title.
2015: India lost to Australia by 95 runs in Sydney on March 26; Steve Smith scored 105 in 93 balls and Australia made 328 for 7.
2019: India lost to New Zealand by 18 runs in Manchester after restricting them to 239 for 8; Ravindra Jadeja scored 77 and MS Dhoni 50.
Matt Henry was Man-of-the-Match in the 2019 semi-final, dismissing KL Rahul and Rohit Sharma early.
India were playing the Netherlands in their ninth round-robin match at M Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru on November 12, 2023.
